summary: The Green hand-off command passes, but a new adversarial test exposes an invalid inventory false PASS. Identically renaming a sound in both input folders makes the script produce a hand-off missing the required filename. The committed test fails against the audited implementation.
blocking_findings: ADV-P5-1 [Blocker] adversarial-testing: scripts/audio-handoff.mjs:17-33 checks only inventory counts and source/demo name equality. In an isolated fixture, renaming tap.ogg to tap-renamed.ogg in both folders makes the script exit 0 and write tap-renamed.ogg instead of tap.ogg. This can deliver a wrong file set to the PM. Require the exact 14 supported names before writing.
evidence: The exact Green command exited 0: the hand-off generator ran, 8 tests passed, sha256sum verified 14 files, and the before/after monorepo status lists were identical.
The copied-fixture rename probe exited 0 and created tap-renamed.ogg in the hand-off output, while the required tap.ogg was absent.
The committed adversarial test fails first against the audited script: expected a nonzero status for the unsupported inventory, received exit 0.
The project gate ran once and exited 1: 1 failed, 3,386 passed, and 8 skipped across 230 files. The only failure was the new adversarial inventory test.
In copied folders, a flipped source byte, a deleted file, and an extra file each made the script exit 1.
The script ran twice over a dirty copied output folder, removed the stale file, and produced exactly 17 files each time. It also succeeded when the sibling monorepo path was absent.
Recomputed SHA-256 values, byte sizes, and target values matched all 14 manifest rows. Swapping a checksum filename made sha256sum -c exit 1.
The original hand-off test failed when the copied documentation row named example.invalid/audio/ instead of the proposed target.
The Phase 5 plan has no A5 false-claim phrase. The reviewed script and tests have no A7-style English-word exclusion filter.
